high.title: Prime Minister Requests SBV to Research Real Estate Classification for Credit Limit Regulations
high.summary: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung directed the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) on April 29 to proactively monitor domestic and international financial and monetary market developments, including monetary policy adjustments by central banks and major economies. The PM emphasized the need for enhanced analytical and forecasting capabilities to ensure timely, flexible, and effective policy responses. Key directives include implementing proactive and flexible monetary policy coordination with fiscal and other macro policies, maintaining stable and appropriate interest rate levels, and directing credit institutions to further reduce operational costs and increase technology adoption. Critically for FX and credit markets, the PM requested SBV to urgently review and study amendments to regulations, particularly researching real estate classification systems to establish appropriate credit limits. This suggests potential tightening of real estate lending regulations, which could impact bank credit growth and VND liquidity conditions.

high.title: Two Scenarios for Vietnamese Stock Market During "Sell in May" Month
high.summary: April 2026 marked a pivotal shift for Vietnamese stock market from "defensive" to "explosive" mode following FTSE Russell's confirmation that Vietnam passed the review and will be officially upgraded in September 2026. The VN-Index recovered strongly, breaking through technical resistance levels near historical peaks. However, average trading liquidity dropped 20% to VND 24.3 trillion in April compared to March, partly due to rising deposit rates (commonly 8-9%, touching 10% for long-term deposits), drawing funds back to savings channels. VFS Securities outlines two May scenarios: Scenario 1 (50% probability) sees VN-Index continuing upward momentum with strong foreign inflows ahead of the upgrade, while Scenario 2 involves consolidation due to high interest rates and liquidity concerns. The analysis highlights how rising deposit rates are creating competition for equity investment flows, a critical factor for FX stability as domestic savings vs. investment dynamics shift.

medium.title: One Bank Set to Pay 20.5% Dividend
medium.summary: SeABank's AGM approved increasing charter capital to VND 34.688 trillion through issuing 583.8 million shares for 20.5% stock dividend and 40 million shares for ESOP. The bank targets 2026 pre-tax profit of VND 7.068 trillion (up 3%), total asset growth of 10%, deposit growth of 23%, and credit growth of 17%, maintaining ROE at 13.0%.

medium.title: Banking Sector Q1/2026 Results Update: VietinBank Surprises
medium.summary: VietinBank reported consolidated pre-tax profit of VND 11.139 trillion in Q1/2026, up 63% YoY, with total assets rising 5.7% to over VND 2.92 quadrillion. Customer loans increased 1.8% to exceed VND 2 quadrillion. NPL ratio improved from 1.1% to 1.02%. MB recorded pre-tax profit of VND 9.628 trillion with credit growth of 3.4% and deposit decline of 1.7%.

medium.title: Latest Forecast for Deposit Rates After April 30 Holiday
medium.summary: SNI Credit Rating notes that rising interest rates and tight liquidity remain major concerns in banking sector AGMs. Despite expectations for deposit rate cooling after early April SBV-bank meetings, funding pressure persists, limiting prospects for significant short-term rate cuts. VPBank CEO cited high Q1 deposit rate increases due to market liquidity stress and strong credit growth.

medium.title: Hoa Phat Must Bear VND 15 Billion in Interest Daily as "Money Mountain" at Banks Surges
medium.summary: Hoa Phat recorded record interest expenses of over VND 1.333 trillion in Q1/2026, averaging nearly VND 15 billion daily, double YoY and 14% higher QoQ. The company attributed rising costs to ending capitalization after Dung Quat 2 operations began and persistently high VND lending rates due to supply-demand imbalances forcing banks to raise deposit rates.

medium.title: World Gold Prices Suddenly Drop Rapidly on Evening of May 1
medium.summary: International gold prices fell $70/ounce to $4,561 on May 1 evening after recovering above $4,630 in morning trading. Unusually, both gold and USD declined simultaneously, with DXY Index breaking below 98 points to 97.9 - lowest in 2 months. Oil also cooled to $110/barrel. TD Securities notes gold affected by Middle East oil supply shocks driving inflation concerns.
